output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, the newest identified consumer class action is Howell v. Costco Wholesale Corp., filed November 6 in New York, alleging tariff-related overcharges that Costco should refund. An October 22 case, Bovenberg v. Costco Wholesale Corporation, invokes the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. Recent resolutions include the October 16 dismissal with prejudice of the Kirkland “100% agave” tequila case and an approved Washington marketing-email settlement exceeding $14 million, reported October 8. Other recent proposed class actions challenge Kirkland “sugar-free” electrolyte labeling and Costco’s ethical-sourcing representations concerning child and forced labor. Costco’s FY2026 annual report also discloses continuing opioid, employee second-job restriction, website-tracking/privacy and earlier tariff-refund litigation.
caveats: The allegations are not findings of wrongdoing, and a proposed class action does not itself establish class certification. The ethical-sourcing account cited here is from plaintiffs’ counsel.

The tequila case was dismissed with prejudice, while the Washington email case reached an approved settlement; they should not be described as newly pending claims. Costco denied wrongdoing in the email case.
This is a selected overview, not a complete list of Costco’s lawsuits. Statuses reflect the cited reporting and disclosures; later docket developments may not be captured.

The court dismissed with prejudice Salisbury v. Costco, which challenged the “100% de Agave” labeling of Kirkland tequila.
The Seattle Times reported final approval of a settlement requiring Costco to pay more than $14 million over allegedly misleading marketing emails; Costco denied wrongdoing.
KIRO 7 reported Mason Maldonado’s proposed class action challenging “sugar-free” claims for Kirkland Signature Hydration Electrolyte Drink Mix because it contains allulose.
Plaintiffs’ counsel announced an Oregon proposed consumer class action alleging misleading ethical-sourcing and child- and forced-labor prevention representations.
In its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended August 30, 2026, Costco disclosed remaining opioid-related lawsuits and said it was defending the pending matters.
The FY2026 Form 10-K disclosed the Gray employee class action alleging unlawful restrictions on second jobs.
The FY2026 Form 10-K disclosed website pixel-tracking/privacy litigation and earlier consumer tariff-refund class actions.
